suggestions.quote: the biggest number tells you what is likely; it cannot tell you what is worth choosing
suggestions.fix: This reads like a teacher's thesis. Break it for the ear and keep the full-sentence landing: "The biggest number? It tells you what's likely. Not what's worth choosing." Direction: quiet, almost amused, after the beat with his dark chip.

suggestions.quote: Row three. You don't look up. Out in the lane: thwack.
suggestions.fix: Keep it as the last line. Direct it warm and low, with a real beat before "thwack" so the sound effect carries it. Give "thwack" its own take, or let the effect replace the word. The colon will not be heard, so write it as "Out in the lane... thwack."

suggestions.quote: nought point nought four per cent
suggestions.fix: Put in say.yaml as "zero point zero four per cent", the form style.md uses ("zero point four five") and the one Riya says. Use the same "zero" for the cousin's chip at line 35 ("zero point two per cent"). Direction: hushed, flat, stunned.
Say.yaml: "sixty-one per cent", read as a half-laugh, amused and disbelieving, so the reversal lands. Keep "three per cent" for the teacher dry and flat, and make the gap between the two audible.

A one-word line that needs its own take, hushed and warm with a held breath after it, because the cruelty is that it sounds kind. Give it 1.0x with no tempo lift and cut straight into the wordless peak.

suggestions.quote: the hall becomes one lit chair among two thousand five hundred
suggestions.fix: For the ear, say it as a question answered at once: "Zero point zero four per cent. What's that, in people? One chair. Out of two thousand five hundred." Direction: curious, then hushed on "one chair".

suggestions.quote: Therefore you trust the topper, but her chip is for music, not the exam.
suggestions.fix: In the script, keep the spoken version in fragments and do not write "therefore" as a spoken word. Use e.g. "The topper, then. Surely. ...Her chip says music. Not the exam." Direction: wry, with a small drop on "music".
